question: What does the Matrice 30T manual say about altitude and obstacles during Failsafe RTH?

intake.focus: altitude and obstacles during Failsafe RTH
intake.reason: Question about what the Matrice 30T manual says regarding Failsafe Return-To-Home altitude and obstacle handling.

brief.short_answer: The manual says RTH altitude is tied to the Home Point and must be higher than any obstacle in the area. It also states the aircraft cannot avoid obstacles during failsafe RTH when there is insufficient light. During RTH, continue to monitor liveview and the aircraft altitude in case failsafe is disabled due to GNSS signal dropping below three bars.

claims.text: The manual states that the RTH altitude is related to the Home Point. Make sure the RTH altitude is higher than any obstacle in the area.
claims.quote: The RTH altitude is related to the Home Point. Make sure the RTH altitude is higher than any obstacle in the area.

claims.text: The aircraft cannot avoid obstacles during failsafe RTH when there is insufficient light.
claims.quote: The aircraft cannot avoid obstacles during failsafe RTH when there is insufficient light.

claims.text: During RTH, continue to check the liveview and the aircraft altitude in case failsafe is disabled due to the GNSS signal icon having less than three bars.
claims.quote: During RTH, continue to check the liveview and the aircraft altitude in case failsafe is disabled due to the GNSS signal icon having less than three bars.
conditions: failsafe may be disabled due to GNSS signal with less than three bars

gaps.text: There is no claimed rule in the manual about obstacle avoidance during failsafe RTH under low light.
No explicit manual statement that liveview should remain unchecked during RTH if failsafe is active.
It is unclear how RTH altitude requirements interact with GNSS signal status and liveview checks.

C001.rationale: The cited passage states that the RTH altitude is related to the Home Point and that the RTH altitude should be higher than any obstacle in the area, which matches the claim.

C002.rationale: The passage explicitly states that the aircraft cannot avoid obstacles during failsafe RTH when there is insufficient light.
